info.title: A2E Developer API
info.description:
A2E.AI provides affordable, accessible, and flexible AI-powered media processing capabilities through RESTful APIs. Generate avatar videos, swap faces, clone voices, create images and videos from text or images, and much more.

## Quickstart for AI Integration

Use the machine-readable OpenAPI spec or download a generated SKILL.md for Cursor, MCP clients, and other AI agents.

| Resource | URL |
|----------|-----|
| OpenAPI JSON | [`https://video.a2e.ai/dev/openapi-spec`](https://video.a2e.ai/dev/openapi-spec) |
| SKILL.md | [`https://video.a2e.ai/dev/skill`](https://video.a2e.ai/dev/skill) |
| Webhook receiver | [Receiving protocol](https://video.a2e.ai/dev#description/webhook-receiving-protocol) |
| Get API Token | [Account > API Token](https://video.a2e.ai/account/token) |

**3-step quickstart:**
1. Create an API token in **Account > API Token**.
2. Load the machine-readable OpenAPI spec from `https://video.a2e.ai/dev/openapi-spec`
3. Download the generated SKILL.md from `https://video.a2e.ai/dev/skill`

## Minimal image-to-video integration

1. Call POST /v1/r2/upload-presigned-url with a unique key, contentType and the actual file size (or omit a size binding). Read data.uploadUrl and data.cdnUrl.
2. PUT the actual file bytes to data.uploadUrl with the same Content-Type and, when bound, the actual Content-Length. Continue only after the PUT succeeds; use data.cdnUrl as image_url.
3. Quote POST /v1/userImage2Video/start through POST /v1/generation/quote with endpoint and the exact requestBody: name, image_url, prompt, model_version=a2e, video_time=5. Continue only when code=0 and data.available=true. A quote does not reserve credits or validate access.
4. Submit that same requestBody to POST /v1/userImage2Video/start. Check code and save data._id. A successful moderation response may have no task ID; do not poll such a response.
5. Poll GET /v1/userImage2Video/{_id} at a modest interval, such as 10 seconds, until current_status is completed or failed. On completion, download result_url before expirationDate; on failure, surface failed_code and failed_message and consult hasRefundCoin rather than assuming a refund.

Example generation body after replacing the accessible image_url:

    {"name":"API example","image_url":"https://example.com/input.jpg","prompt":"A gentle camera move","model_version":"a2e","video_time":5}

Use this exact object as requestBody when quoting and as the submission body. Replace the image URL with data.cdnUrl from your successful PUT; the placeholder image URL is not an uploaded asset.

Other models use their documented ID, status, result and billing fields; do not apply this workflow's field names to every model. Quote, submission and final settlement are separate stages. The OpenAPI license metadata alone is not a license for hosted services, third-party models or generated outputs; consult their applicable terms.

## Access Points

| Environment | Base URL |
|--------|----------|
| Current Environment | `https://api.a2e.ai` |

## Authentication

Use an **API token** for developer API calls.
API tokens start with `sk_` and should be sent as a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header.

### How to get an API token

1. Sign in to `https://video.a2e.ai`.
2. Open **Account > API Token**.
3. Create a new token and copy the generated value.
4. Send it in the request header as `Authorization: Bearer sk_...`.

JWT/session tokens used by the web app are not part of the public developer authentication flow and are not required in this documentation.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.a2e.ai/v1/..." \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "my-task", "prompt": "..."}'
```

## Webhook receiving protocol

For generation operations that accept `webhook_url`, submit with an API token and an optional `webhook_token` (your shared secret). Browser/session requests cannot configure callbacks. The URL must normally be a public HTTPS address without URL credentials; private and reserved hosts/IPs are rejected, and the host is checked again before delivery. Local development has limited HTTP exceptions. The token is limited to 256 visible ASCII characters and is never returned in task details or callback bodies; `webhook_token_set` indicates whether one was configured.

On a terminal result, we make one best-effort HTTP POST to your URL with `Content-Type: application/json`. The JSON body is the formatted **task object itself**, not the detail API's `{code,data}` envelope and not `{event,data}`. Task fields vary by generation family; use the task ID and X-A2e-Event header as the common terminal signal. Most task families expose current_status (completed/failed/blocked; blocked is delivered as task.failed), while legacy Video exposes status (success/fail). Consult that family's detail operation for result fields. Some detail endpoints add computed fields that do not appear in callbacks. Event metadata is in headers:

| Header | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `X-A2e-Event` | `task.completed` or `task.failed` |
| `X-A2e-Task-Type` | Task family identifier; do not assume it equals an OpenAPI tag |
| `X-A2e-Webhook-Token` | Your configured shared token, when supplied |

For a current_status task family, a minimal completed body: `{"_id":"507f1f77bcf86cd799439011","current_status":"completed"}` with `X-A2e-Event: task.completed`. A minimal failed body for that family: `{"_id":"507f1f77bcf86cd799439012","current_status":"failed"}` with `X-A2e-Event: task.failed`. These illustrate one task family; actual task objects contain family-specific fields. Check the shared token against your stored value and deduplicate by task ID before processing. No HMAC signature is sent.

Return any 2xx response after accepting the event. The sender times out after 5 seconds, does not follow redirects, and limits request and response bodies to 64 KiB. A non-2xx response, timeout, or delivery failure is **not retried**. Poll the task detail API to recover a missed event; the detail response is the source of truth. Callbacks are only attempted for eligible API-token tasks with a configured URL and are not sent for intermediate states.

## Errors, retries, and task deletion

Read both the HTTP status and JSON `code`. A normal `ctx.success` response is HTTP 200 with `code: 0`; a business error can be HTTP 200 with a nonzero `code` and `msg`. Other validation, authorization, missing-task, and server errors can use HTTP 4xx/5xx. Do not treat every HTTP 200 as a successful task submission. A top-level `trace_id`, when present, identifies the request for support and is not a task ID; include it with the HTTP status, code, and task ID when reporting a problem.

| Condition | Client action |
|-----------|---------------|
| Invalid input, missing access, or insufficient balance (for example `100000`, `100004`, `20003`) | Fix the input, permissions, or balance before another submission. |
| Task still processing (`30101`) | Poll its detail endpoint; do not resubmit or repeatedly DELETE. |
| Task not found (`30104`) | Check the task ID, account, and whether it was deleted. |
| Temporary HTTP 5xx or network failure on a read | Retry the read with bounded exponential backoff and jitter. |

For detail polling, start around 3–5 seconds and back off toward 30 seconds with jitter; this is client guidance, not a guaranteed service interval or request-rate allowance. Account-level generation concurrency and HTTP request-rate limits are separate controls. Follow an explicit `Retry-After` if one is returned. Avoid simultaneous polling bursts across many tasks.

Paid creation POSTs have no documented idempotency-key guarantee. If a POST times out or its response is lost, the task may already exist and have been charged. Do not automatically replay it: first reconcile recent task/list and billing records using the submitted time and task details, then decide whether a new submission is needed. A repeated POST can create and charge for a second task.

DELETE is not a universal cancellation operation. The task families below follow different code paths; a 200 DELETE response does not by itself promise cancellation, immediate physical media removal, or a refund.

| Task family | Allowed state and window | Deletion and refund |
|-------------|--------------------------|---------------------|
| Head Swap, Image to Video, Face Swap Task, and other media tasks using the shared task-delete path | initialized only after at least 60 seconds from creation; completed, failed, blocked (including legacy block) at any time. sent, pending, and processing are rejected. | Soft-delete; refund only a qualifying queued initialized task. |
| Video Twin | initialized only after 60 seconds; completed or failed at any time. Other states are rejected. | Soft-delete; refund an eligible queued task or a record with a pending billing refund. |
| Photobook | initialized, completed, or failed, subject to an in-flight claim check; no fixed 60-second rule. | Soft-delete; refund initialized or pending-refund records. |
| Sora 2 Pro | sent, pending, and processing are rejected; no fixed 60-second rule for initialized. | Soft-delete; refund initialized if it has not already been refunded. |
| GPT Image, Flux 2, Kling Image, Qwen Image, Wan 2.6/2.7 Image | No processing-state gate in the history-delete path. | Set deleted=true; no cancellation or refund in that path. |
| Kling Video, Kling Omni, Seedance 1.5/2.0 | No processing-state gate in the owned-record delete path. | Soft-delete; no cancellation or refund in that path. |

Other DELETE endpoints, including voice and asset records, have their own lifecycle rules. Read each operation description before applying a task-family rule to it.

## FAQ

**What is the SLA?**
No measured uptime period or contractual SLA is published in this reference. Consult the current service terms and support for availability commitments.

**Is there a free tier?**
Signup credit eligibility and amounts depend on current site settings. Credits do not grant access to every model: paid-access rules still apply, and an API token does not bypass them. Browser-only quotas are not automatically available to API-token requests. Check current pricing and the generation response before treating an operation as free.

post.description:
Legacy endpoint for generating a pre-signed PUT URL.
Prefer /v1/r2/upload-presigned-url for new integrations.
If bucket is omitted, files are uploaded to 3days-apac by default. The returned uploadUrl may use R2 or Amazon S3 and contains the authentication needed for the PUT; an S3 upload's cdnUrl is served through CloudFront. Use the returned uploadUrl and cdnUrl without reconstructing or changing their hosts, paths or query strings.
urlPrefix requests a leading object-key path.
cdnDomain requests a CDN domain suffix for R2 uploads.
The returned logical key is scoped to {urlPrefix}/{env}/user/{user_id}/. CloudFront URLs and physical S3 object keys additionally include the jp-s3/{bucket}/ routing prefix.
PUT upload contract (also applies to the legacy alias):
- Only the A2E request for this URL uses Authorization: Bearer. Send the raw file bytes to uploadUrl with HTTP PUT; do not use JSON or multipart/form-data.
- The uploadUrl query already authenticates the PUT. Use a separate unauthenticated HTTP client: do not forward Authorization or manually add x-amz-* headers.
- Send Content-Type matching the requested contentType. Preserve the complete uploadUrl, including all query bytes and its storage host; do not rewrite it to cdnUrl.
- fileSize and contentLength are optional outside site runtimes. Omit them for a minimal upload; never copy a placeholder byte count.
- If you provide a positive integer size, Content-Length must equal that actual file byte count. Outside site runtimes, contentLength takes priority over fileSize; site runtimes ignore contentLength and always bind the PUT to the validated fileSize. A chunked request without that bound Content-Length will fail.
- Site runtimes can require fileSize; use the actual byte count there. expiresIn is URL validity, not object retention. Use cdnUrl only after PUT succeeds.
- Browser clients may set forceR2=true only when retrying a failed S3 PUT. This bypasses the S3 sample for that replacement upload target.
Two-step cURL example (requires curl and jq):
```sh
curl -X POST "https://api.a2e.ai/v1/r2/get_upload_presigned_url" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_A2E_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"key":"upload.png","purpose":"STAGING","contentType":"image/png","expiresIn":300}' \
  --fail-with-body --output /tmp/a2e-upload-response.json
upload_url=$(jq -er '.data.uploadUrl' /tmp/a2e-upload-response.json)
curl -X PUT "$upload_url" -H 'Content-Type: image/png' \
  --data-binary @upload.png --fail-with-body
```
Replace YOUR_A2E_API_KEY and upload.png with your own API key and file.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Send an `application/json` body. Required fields: `key`.
### Behavior
- Validates the submitted payload and performs the operation described by the request schema.
- Conditional fields, mutually exclusive inputs, limits, and defaults are enforced as documented by their schemas.
### Response
- On `200`, consume the fields defined by that response schema below.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.
### Errors
- `400` — Bad Request - Invalid parameters.
- `401` — Unauthorized - Invalid or missing JWT token.
### Related Operations
- `POST /v1/r2/upload-presigned-url` — Get pre-signed upload URL.

bucket.description: R2 bucket. Defaults to 3days-apac. Deprecated, use purpose instead.

purpose.description: Storage purpose. The backend maps it to the physical bucket. Ignored when bucket is provided.

urlPrefix.description: Leading object-key path. Defaults to adam2eve.

cdnDomain.description: CDN domain suffix without scheme or path.

contentType.description: MIME type to bind to the upload request.

fileSize.description: Optional actual file size in bytes. A positive safe integer binds Content-Length; the PUT must send exactly this many raw bytes.

contentLength.description: Optional actual Content-Length in bytes. A positive safe integer binds the PUT length; takes priority over fileSize outside site runtimes. Site runtimes ignore it and sign with fileSize.

forceR2.description: Bypass the S3 sample and return an R2 upload target. Intended for retrying a failed S3 PUT.

401.description: Unauthorized - Invalid or missing bearer token

post.description:
Talking Photo and Talking Video use the same capped audio-duration calculator as submission. freeVideoDurationSeconds means audio seconds for these modes. Authentication requirements are unchanged.
Returns a credit estimate without creating a task, calling a generation provider, or charging credits.
For agent use, send `endpoint` plus the exact `requestBody` intended for that generation endpoint.
Only pricing-related fields are interpreted; a successful quote does not validate the complete generation request.
The legacy normalized quote body remains supported for backward compatibility.
Seedream 5.5 layer decomposition is charged at the configured max_images upper limit (default 5), not the actual returned count. Fewer layers do not receive a partial refund; auto resolution is charged at the 2K tier.
Core first-last-frame video quotes preserve the requested batch size (`requestBody.number_of_images`, or legacy `count`) and multiply the per-output price by that count, matching generation billing.
Unlimited mode still quotes one output; its video price is zero and optional V1 auto-audio is charged once. V2 models do not support Unlimited mode.
Only supported generation endpoints can be quoted. `/v1/seedAudio/generate` and `/v1/seedAudio/start` do not support advance quotes because the actual output duration is only known after generation.
`/v1/video/send_tts` is billed after synthesis by the actual audio duration; its quote estimates the duration from the text length (about 4 CJK characters or 2.5 words per second, adjusted by `speechRate`) and returns `exact: false` with `estimated: true`.
Seed Audio reserves 120 credits at submission and settles against the actual output duration after success; the reservation is not an estimate of the final charge. Explain the billing rules and obtain the user's acceptance before submitting generation directly.
HTTP 400 with `code=UNSUPPORTED_GENERATION_QUOTE_ENDPOINT` is a non-retryable capability response, not a generation failure. Do not repeatedly request a quote for the same unsupported endpoint.
For A2E/Qwen image generation, include the output `width` and `height` as well as `resolution`.
For `/v1/talkingVideo/start`, include `input_audio_duration` in `requestBody` to quote the source audio length; `input_video_duration` does not price this operation.
For `/v1/talkingPhoto/start`, include `product_version` and `input_audio_duration` in `requestBody`; V2 quotes 4–300 seconds at its own rate. In a normalized talking-photo quote, use `productVersion` and `inputVideoDuration`.
In the legacy normalized quote body, use `inputAudioDuration` for Talking Video. `inputVideoDuration` remains accepted as a legacy alias and is interpreted as audio duration for that mode.
`/v1/imageBackgroundRemoval/start` uses GPT Image 2.5 Flare pricing at the requested `resolution` (default `1K`).
Quotes use the same dimension-based resolution promotion as task creation. A2E V1 supports `1K`, `1080P`, and `2K`; V2 accepts legacy `1K` as `1080P` and supports `1080P` and `2K` output.
V2 fractional `width` and `height` values are rounded before both quote and submission; V2 text-to-image quotes accept the same `21:9` aspect ratio as task creation, and ratios beyond 21:9 are rejected before charging.
A quote is not a task, entitlement approval, balance reservation, or payment. Even available=true/generationRequestValidated=false does not guarantee submission will be accepted. Use /v1/feature-pricing for the current configured price source; user role and current site basic settings determine access. API tokens do not bypass paid-access gates. Free signup credits do not grant access to every model.
For duration-priced media operations, include the measured source duration (input_audio_duration for talkingVideo, input_video_duration for video transforms). For a signed-in web Actor Swap quote, video_url can be used for server-side duration probing when input_video_duration is unavailable; API-token callers still need to provide the duration. HTTP 200 with available=false must be resolved before submission.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Send an `application/json` body when using the optional controls documented in the request schema.
### Behavior
- Validates the submitted payload and performs the operation described by the request schema.
- Conditional fields, mutually exclusive inputs, limits, and defaults are enforced as documented by their schemas.
### Response
- On `200`, consume the fields defined by that response schema below.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.
### Errors
- `400` — Unsupported endpoint or invalid pricing combinations. Missing duration may instead return HTTP 200 with available=false; inspect data.available.
- `401` — Missing or invalid bearer token.

Authentication: set header Authorization: Bearer <token> (supports user JWT or sk_ API token).

schema.description: Use endpoint plus requestBody, OR a legacy normalized body with mode. Endpoint/requestBody takes precedence when supplied.

endpoint.description: Generation route path. A leading `POST ` is accepted but optional.

requestBody.description: The exact JSON body intended for the generation request.

count.description: Batch size. Most models accept 1-8; `kling-image-3.0` and `seedream-5.5` accept 1-9. The former maps to `n` on `/v1/userKlingImage/start`; the latter creates separate text-to-image tasks.

model.description: Required for video/image model modes. Prefer endpoint/requestBody instead of guessing normalized model names.

productVersion.description: Talking Photo model version in a normalized quote; defaults to v1.

inputVideoCount.description: Kling 4.0 supports up to five videos; other normalized models retain their own limits. For Kling 4.0, provide inputVideoUrls or owned elementIds for server-verified durations. hasVideoInput or inputVideoDuration alone returns available=false.

inputVideoUrls.description: Uploaded Kling 4.0 input videos, probed server-side for exact pricing.

elementIds.description: Owned Kling 4.0 elements; video element durations are resolved server-side.

200.description: Estimate result. HTTP 200 with available=false and coins=null means no usable estimate, never a free generation.

exact.description: Present for endpoint/requestBody form only. Pricing exactness does not validate the complete generation request.

estimated.description: Present when the price is estimated from text length because the final charge depends on the generated output (text-to-speech).

generationRequestValidated.description: Present for endpoint/requestBody form; quote only interprets pricing inputs.

freeQuotaCoins.description: Expected credit discount for this request, as returned by the quote.

freeQuotaApplied.description: Optional web-account quota result; API-token requests do not inherit browser-only quota.

trace_id.description: Trace ID of this HTTP request. Include it when contacting support about this request. It is generated per request and is not a task identifier; use the returned task `_id` to query results.

400.description: Unsupported endpoint or invalid pricing combinations. Missing duration may instead return HTTP 200 with available=false; inspect data.available.

401.description: Missing or invalid bearer token

Returns the system and user-specific avatars available to the authenticated API user.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Send an `application/json` body when using the optional controls documented in the request schema.
### Behavior
- Returns the collection visible in the current request and authorization context.
- Apply the documented pagination and filter parameters when present; use response metadata to continue paging.
- Record fields and status values have the same meaning as in the corresponding detail operation.
### Response
- The `200` response contains the requested collection in the response envelope documented below.
- An empty collection is a successful result when no matching records are available.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.
### Errors
- `400` — Bad Request - Invalid parameters.
- `401` — Unauthorized - Invalid or missing JWT token.

Authentication: set header Authorization: Bearer <token> (supports user JWT or sk_ API token).

web_type.description: Optional client type. Use a2e or tyzn to include default system avatars alongside user-specific avatars.

401.description: Unauthorized - Invalid or missing bearer token

get.summary: Get a downloadable video URL from a share link
get.description:
Accepts a complete /share-result/{shareId} link. Returns the current result video URL for a completed, unexpired shared task without downloading media through this API. The returned URL may expire; save the file before expires_at when present. Image shares, expired shares, and results without a video URL return an error.
### Request
- This operation does not declare bearer authentication in the published specification.
- Supported query parameters: `share_url`. Omitted values use the defaults shown in the parameter schema.
### Behavior
- Reads the requested information without creating a generation task.
- Use the returned fields as documented; availability may depend on the caller and current resource state.
### Response
- On `200`, consume the fields defined by that response schema below.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.
### Errors
- `400` — Malformed or unsupported share link.
- `404` — Shared video is missing, unavailable, or expired.

trace_id.description: Trace ID of this HTTP request. Include it when contacting support about this request. It is generated per request and is not a task identifier; use the returned task `_id` to query results.

404.description: Shared video is missing, unavailable, or expired.

parameters.name: share_url
parameters.description: Complete share-result link issued by this service.

post.description:
Convert text to speech using AI voices with customizable parameters.
### Voice Selection
Provide exactly one of `tts_id` (system voice) or `user_voice_id` (custom cloned voice).
Do not send both: synthesis would use the `tts_id` voice while locale defaults and billing follow `user_voice_id`.
- `tts_id`: Use built-in system voice (400+ voices available)
- `user_voice_id`: Use your own custom cloned voice; omitted `country` and `region` default to `en-US`
### Billing
System voice lists return the current account's `ttsRate` in credits per 10 seconds.
Charges are based on the generated audio duration: `ceil(duration / 10) * ttsRate`.
A valid zero rate means no credits are charged. Fetch the selected voice's current rate before submitting;
generated duration is unknown before synthesis, so this rate is not a total-price quote.
### Text Limitations
- **API token users**: No local 3000-unit text limit is applied by this controller
- **Web users**: Maximum 3000 weighted units after pause tags are removed
- The server counts ASCII and Latin-1 characters as one unit, Cyrillic characters as one unit, and other non-Latin-1 characters as two units

Retry an owned, non-deleted task with _id, or a batch with _ids.
When both are supplied, _ids takes precedence. Batch IDs are deduplicated
case-insensitively and results retain their first-occurrence order.
Records are queried in chunks of 50 and submissions run with at most four
concurrent tasks per request. There is no new request-size limit; an empty
batch succeeds without submitting work. All batch items are awaited, even
after failures. Any failure preserves the top-level error code and HTTP
status of the first failed item in input order; data.results also includes
successful items so clients can avoid resubmitting them.

- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.

- Requests another processing attempt for an eligible failed task.
- Eligibility, charging, and state transitions follow the task-specific rules exposed by the response.

post.description:
Retry an owned, non-deleted task with _id, or a batch with _ids.
When both are supplied, _ids takes precedence. Batch IDs are deduplicated
case-insensitively and results retain their first-occurrence order.
Records are queried in chunks of 50 and submissions run with at most four
concurrent tasks per request. There is no new request-size limit; an empty
batch succeeds without submitting work. All batch items are awaited, even
after failures. Any failure preserves the top-level error code and HTTP
status of the first failed item in input order; data.results also includes
successful items so clients can avoid resubmitting them.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Send an `application/json` body when using the optional controls documented in the request schema.
### Behavior
- Requests another processing attempt for an eligible failed task.
- Eligibility, charging, and state transitions follow the task-specific rules exposed by the response.
- Continue monitoring the same or returned task identifier after the retry is accepted.
### Response
- A `200` response confirms task acceptance; it does not by itself mean media generation has completed.
- Retain the returned identifier and wait for a documented terminal status before using output URLs.

post.description:
Create one or more asynchronous text-to-image tasks, then return the records used to monitor generated images.
Select the image model with `model_type`:
- `a2e`: auto-select the default image model. It supports text-to-image and image editing with up to two reference images.
- `a2e-v2`: use the V2 image algorithm with the same inputs, output count, pricing, and access rules as `a2e`. It accepts up to two reference images; legacy `1K` requests are billed and generated as `1080P`.
- `zimage`: Z-Image Turbo for text-to-image generation. It does not accept reference images.
- `seedream`: the Seedream image generation and editing family. Set `model_version` to `4.5`, `5.0`, `5.0-pro`, or `5.5`; Seedream 5.0 Pro and 5.5 accept up to ten reference images, while 4.5 and 5.0 accept up to two.
On CN sites, pure text-to-image requests for both `a2e` and `a2e-v2` use Z-Image and its provider content inspection.
Seedream 5.5 supports `background` (auto/transparent/opaque), `output_format` (PNG/JPEG), and optional layer decomposition from exactly one input image. Transparent backgrounds require PNG. A layer request omits `background`, returns one base image and up to 99 transparent PNG layers, and may request OCR metadata. The response includes every layer's URL, order, position and optional recognized text.
API clients should normally set concrete output dimensions with `width` and `height`. The optional `aspect_ratio` and `resolution` fields are also accepted and validated by this endpoint (an unsupported value returns 400), and both are echoed back in the task records, so they are part of the public request contract. For Seedream 5.0 Pro `aspect_ratio` takes precedence over `width`/`height`, and when it is omitted the backend falls back to `9:16`.
Actual media size, dimensions, duration, format and applicable frame-rate limits are checked against the selected provider interface before charging or creating any task. Client metadata is not authoritative. Invalid or unreadable media returns HTTP 400 with the failing field, measured value and expected range; direct API requests are not automatically resized or transcoded and do not inherit lower website upload limits.
Media inspection errors preserve HTTP status and business code: 400 INVALID_MEDIA for confirmed invalid media, 400 MEDIA_RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for inaccessible or expired sources, 400 MEDIA_PROBE_LIMIT for the server source inspection budget, 429 MEDIA_PROBE_BUSY for local queue saturation, 503 MEDIA_PROBE_UNAVAILABLE for transient network/upstream failures, 504 MEDIA_PROBE_TIMEOUT for inspection timeouts, and 500 MEDIA_PROBE_FAILED for internal processing failures. All media checked for this request share a 280-second deadline, including queueing, Range probing and full-download fallback. Even valid assets can exceed this processing deadline. Timeout cancels remaining inspection and cleanup completes before returning; no automatic retry, charge, task creation or generation-provider submission occurs on failed inspection.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Send an `application/json` body. Required fields: `prompt`.
- API-token callers may include `webhook_url` and `webhook_token` for best-effort terminal-state notifications; ordinary JWT/cookie calls ignore these fields.
### Behavior
- This is an asynchronous operation: a successful submission creates a task and returns before processing finishes.
- Persist the returned task identifier and use the corresponding detail or list operation to observe progress.
- Treat the detail endpoint as the source of truth even when webhook delivery is enabled.
### Response
- A `200` response confirms task acceptance; it does not by itself mean media generation has completed.
- Retain the returned identifier and wait for a documented terminal status before using output URLs.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.
### Errors
- `400` — Bad Request - Invalid parameters.
- `401` — Unauthorized - Invalid or missing JWT token.
- `429` — MEDIA_PROBE_BUSY - Local media inspection queue is full or its wait deadline elapsed.
- `500` — MEDIA_PROBE_FAILED - Internal media inspection failure; not a media specification violation.
- `503` — MEDIA_PROBE_UNAVAILABLE - Transient network or upstream failure; retry is allowed.
- `504` — MEDIA_PROBE_TIMEOUT - Media connection, download, inspection or the shared 280-second request inspection deadline elapsed; retry is allowed. This is a processing timeout, not a media specification violation.
### Related Operations
- `GET /v1/userText2Image/allRecords` — Get all text to image records.
- `GET /v1/userText2Image/{_id}` — Get text to image record detail.
- `DELETE /v1/userText2Image/{_id}` — Delete task.

Seedream 5.0 Pro resolves the size from this ratio first and only falls back to `width`/`height` when it is absent, and the backend defaults it to `9:16` for Seedream requests that omit it.

resolution.description:
Output resolution tier. Rejected with 400 when the value is outside this enum.
The billed tier is the higher of this value and the tier inferred from the short side of `width`/`height`, so a large `width`/`height` cannot be billed as a lower tier. `a2e` and `zimage` only have `1K`, `1080P`, and `2K`; `3K`/`4K` are treated as `2K` for them. For Seedream 5.0 Pro the output size comes from `aspect_ratio` plus this tier, so `width`/`height` never raise an explicitly requested tier there.
Effective tiers per Seedream version: `5.0-pro` distinguishes only `1K` and `2K` and treats every other value as `2K`; `4.5` serves `2K`/`4K`; `5.0` serves `2K`/`3K`; `5.5` accepts `1K`/`1.5K`/`2K` and defaults to `2K`. Seedream 5.5 layer decomposition additionally accepts `auto`, which is charged at the 2K tier without reconciliation for fewer layers or smaller output sizes; ordinary generation rejects `auto`.

- Text-to-Image generation with advanced prompt understanding
- Image-to-Image editing (up to 8 references for Flux 2 Pro; up to 10 for Flux 3 Klein)
- Character consistency across multiple images
- Text rendering within images
- High-quality output with professional-grade results

- Usually 20-60 seconds
**Output:**
- Images are stored in R2 storage (3days-apac bucket) and expire 3 days after the task is created (createdAt + 3 days, same as `expirationDate`)
- Download and persist the result to your own storage before it expires; `image_url` is a temporary CDN URL, not a permanent asset address
- Expired tasks are omitted from the list endpoint; the detail endpoint still returns the record with `isExpired: true`, but its media URLs are no longer downloadable.

- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.

Generate or edit images with optional reference images. Each reference image after the first increases the cost. The returned `coins` field reports the credits charged for the task.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Send an `application/json` body. Required fields: `name`, `prompt`.

- Persist the returned task identifier and use the corresponding detail or list operation to observe progress.
- Treat the detail endpoint as the source of truth even when webhook delivery is enabled.
### Response
- A `200` response confirms task acceptance; it does not by itself mean media generation has completed.
- Retain the returned identifier and wait for a documented terminal status before using output URLs.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.

post.description:
Create one or more asynchronous Kling 3.0 image tasks from the prompt and optional reference images, subject to the request's `n` limit.
Actual media size, dimensions, duration, format and applicable frame-rate limits are checked against the selected provider interface before charging or creating any task. Client metadata is not authoritative. Invalid or unreadable media returns HTTP 400 with the failing field, measured value and expected range; direct API requests are not automatically resized or transcoded and do not inherit lower website upload limits.
Media inspection errors preserve HTTP status and business code: 400 INVALID_MEDIA for confirmed invalid media, 400 MEDIA_RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for inaccessible or expired sources, 400 MEDIA_PROBE_LIMIT for the server source inspection budget, 429 MEDIA_PROBE_BUSY for local queue saturation, 503 MEDIA_PROBE_UNAVAILABLE for transient network/upstream failures, 504 MEDIA_PROBE_TIMEOUT for inspection timeouts, and 500 MEDIA_PROBE_FAILED for internal processing failures. All media checked for this request share a 280-second deadline, including queueing, Range probing and full-download fallback. Even valid assets can exceed this processing deadline. Timeout cancels remaining inspection and cleanup completes before returning; no automatic retry, charge, task creation or generation-provider submission occurs on failed inspection.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Send an `application/json` body. Required fields: `name`, `prompt`.
- API-token callers may include `webhook_url` and `webhook_token` for best-effort terminal-state notifications; ordinary JWT/cookie calls ignore these fields.
### Behavior
- This is an asynchronous operation: a successful submission creates a task and returns before processing finishes.
- Persist the returned task identifier and use the corresponding detail or list operation to observe progress.
- Treat the detail endpoint as the source of truth even when webhook delivery is enabled.
### Response
- A `200` response confirms task acceptance; it does not by itself mean media generation has completed.
- Retain the returned identifier and wait for a documented terminal status before using output URLs.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.
### Errors
- `401` — Unauthorized - Invalid or missing JWT token.
- `429` — MEDIA_PROBE_BUSY - Local media inspection queue is full or its wait deadline elapsed.
- `500` — MEDIA_PROBE_FAILED - Internal media inspection failure; not a media specification violation.
- `503` — MEDIA_PROBE_UNAVAILABLE - Transient network or upstream failure; retry is allowed.
- `504` — MEDIA_PROBE_TIMEOUT - Media connection, download, inspection or the shared 280-second request inspection deadline elapsed; retry is allowed. This is a processing timeout, not a media specification violation.

name.description: Name of the image to video task

starting_video_url.description: Existing video to extend; the server validates its duration and I2V-compatible parameters.

unlimited.description: Web-only legacy plan-waiver option for a2e; unavailable for V2 models. API token requests with unlimited=true return HTTP 403 with code UNLIMITED_WEB_ONLY.

easy_mode.description: Compatibility easy-mode option for the original a2e image-to-video model; unavailable for V2 and reference modes.

image_url.description: URL of the source image. Required for image-to-video; omit for text-to-video and reference-to-video.

prompt.example: Make the person in the image wave their hand

negative_prompt.description: Optional negative prompt to avoid unwanted features. If omitted, generation service defaults apply. An empty string is accepted.

lora.description: Lora ID. If provided, prompt/negative_prompt can be omitted (prompt will be overwritten by lora preset on backend).

generation_mode.description: Generation mode. Text and reference modes require a2e-v2 or a2e-v2-flash and a nonempty prompt up to 2000 characters. Reference mode accepts video_time of 3, 4, 5, 10 or 15; text mode accepts 5, 10 or 15.

generation_params.description: Text/reference parameters. Omit for image-to-video. Reference mode requires at least one asset; text mode accepts none.

reference_assets.description: At most 9 images, 3 videos and 3 audio files. Video and audio clips must each last 2–15 seconds, with at most 15 seconds total per type.

asset_id.description: Unique reference identifier, such as image_1, video_1 or audio_1.

duration_seconds.description: Required for audio. Video duration is measured by the server.

model_version.description: Algorithm model version. When omitted, Ultra users default to a2e-v2 and other roles default to a2e. a2e-v2 costs more per second; a2e-v2-flash uses a2e pricing. V2 models are not covered by plan waivers.

auto_add_audio.description: Whether to add audio. Defaults to false for a2e (paid ThinkSound post-processing) and true for a2e-v2/a2e-v2-flash (native audio with no ThinkSound surcharge).

end_image_url.description: End image URL (required for FLF2V model)

extend_prompt.description: Whether to extend the prompt automatically

number_of_images.description: Number of videos to generate at once

video_time.description: Video time in integer seconds. Image to video and first-last-frame (FLF2V) accept any integer from 3 to 20; video extension (starting_video_url) supports 5 to 20. Reference mode supports 3, 4, 5, 10 or 15 seconds; text mode supports 5, 10 or 15. Billing uses the effective duration: in image to video, first-last-frame and video extension, a non-zero video_length takes precedence over video_time and is converted to whole seconds by dividing by the model frame rate (16 fps for a2e, 24 fps for a2e-v2 and a2e-v2-flash) and rounding down, then clamped to the mode minimum (3 seconds, or 5 for video extension) and to 20 seconds (for example, 107 frames on a2e-v2 bills 4 seconds, 1 frame bills 3 seconds and 1000 frames bills 20 seconds); otherwise video_time is used. Text and reference modes accept only video_time and reject video_length with HTTP 400. a2e 3- and 4-second videos use 49/65 frames at 16 fps; above 5 seconds a2e generates in 5-second segments, so its output is rounded up to the next multiple of 5 seconds (for example, 6 seconds yields about 10 seconds). a2e-v2 and a2e-v2-flash generate one continuous 24 fps clip whose frame count is rounded up to the next supported 17k+5 frame count, so the output is up to about 0.7 seconds longer than the requested time (for example, 3 seconds yields about 3.04 seconds and 4 seconds yields about 4.46 seconds).

video_length.description: (Deprecated) Video length in frames. Prefer video_time. Backend converts frames to seconds internally.

skip_face_enhance.description: Whether to skip face similarity enhancement. Defaults to false (enhancing face similarity).

mask_face.description: Web NSFW preflight result. Set true only after the user confirms masking a detected human face.

minor_suspected_skip.description: Accepted for backward compatibility only. This endpoint has no backend CSAM detection; moderation comes from the algorithm upstream and this flag is not forwarded to it, so setting it does not bypass an upstream 1004.

watermark_url.description: API only. Public http(s) URL of your own watermark image (any common image format; a PNG with a transparent background looks best), overlaid in the lower-right corner of the generated video. It replaces the default watermark for paid accounts; for free accounts it is ignored and the standard platform watermark rules apply. The image is copied to temporary platform storage and reused for up to 24 hours for the same URL, so changes to the image behind the same URL may take up to 24 hours to apply. If the image cannot be read or applied, the video is still generated without the custom watermark. Omit or send an empty string for no custom watermark. Ignored for web app requests.

post.description:
Start a Wan video generation task. This endpoint supports Wan 2.5 image-to-video, Wan 2.6 image-to-video and Wan 2.7 multi-mode video generation.
For Wan 2.7, set `model` to `wan2.7-i2v` and select the generation mode with `task_type`:
- `text_to_video`: text prompt only. Do not provide image/video material.
- `first_frame`: image-to-video from one first-frame image. Requires `image_url`.
- `first_last_frame`: image-to-video with first and last frame control. Requires `image_url` and `last_frame_url`.
- `reference_image`: reference-to-video. Requires 1 to 5 ordered image/video entries in `reference_media`; legacy pure-image clients may continue using `reference_image_urls`.
- `video_extend`: extend an existing video clip. Requires `first_clip_url`; optional `last_frame_url`.
- `video_edit`: edit an existing video. Requires `edit_video_url`; optional `reference_image_urls` with up to 3 image URLs.
`text_to_video`, `first_last_frame`, `reference_image`, `video_extend` and `video_edit` are only available when `model=wan2.7-i2v`.
Wan 2.7 accepts PNG inputs with or without an alpha channel.
Actual media size, dimensions, duration, format and applicable frame-rate limits are checked against the selected provider interface before charging or creating any task. Client metadata is not authoritative. Invalid or unreadable media returns HTTP 400 with the failing field, measured value and expected range; direct API requests are not automatically resized or transcoded and do not inherit lower website upload limits.
Media inspection errors preserve HTTP status and business code: 400 INVALID_MEDIA for confirmed invalid media, 400 MEDIA_RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for inaccessible or expired sources, 400 MEDIA_PROBE_LIMIT for the server source inspection budget, 429 MEDIA_PROBE_BUSY for local queue saturation, 503 MEDIA_PROBE_UNAVAILABLE for transient network/upstream failures, 504 MEDIA_PROBE_TIMEOUT for inspection timeouts, and 500 MEDIA_PROBE_FAILED for internal processing failures. All media checked for this request share a 280-second deadline, including queueing, Range probing and full-download fallback. Even valid assets can exceed this processing deadline. Timeout cancels remaining inspection and cleanup completes before returning; no automatic retry, charge, task creation or generation-provider submission occurs on failed inspection.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Send an `application/json` body. Required fields: `prompt`.
- API-token callers may include `webhook_url` and `webhook_token` for best-effort terminal-state notifications; ordinary JWT/cookie calls ignore these fields.
### Behavior
- This is an asynchronous operation: a successful submission creates a task and returns before processing finishes.
- Persist the returned task identifier and use the corresponding detail or list operation to observe progress.
- Treat the detail endpoint as the source of truth even when webhook delivery is enabled.
### Response
- A `200` response confirms task acceptance; it does not by itself mean media generation has completed.
- Retain the returned identifier and wait for a documented terminal status before using output URLs.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.
### Errors
- `400` — Bad Request - Invalid parameters.
- `401` — Unauthorized - Invalid or missing JWT token.
- `429` — MEDIA_PROBE_BUSY - Local media inspection queue is full or its wait deadline elapsed.
- `500` — MEDIA_PROBE_FAILED - Internal media inspection failure; not a media specification violation.
- `503` — MEDIA_PROBE_UNAVAILABLE - Transient network or upstream failure; retry is allowed.
- `504` — MEDIA_PROBE_TIMEOUT - Media connection, download, inspection or the shared 280-second request inspection deadline elapsed; retry is allowed. This is a processing timeout, not a media specification violation.

If present, null, malformed, expired or incomplete receipts return AI_SHARING_CONSENT_REQUIRED before generation. Valid receipts cover all actual AI recipients, including safety providers and intermediaries, and constrain later fallback. Content safety checks remain required for native requests. Web and legacy API behavior is unchanged.

post.description:

product_version=v1 uses the existing workflow and requires both prompts. Its billing is capped at 120 seconds.
TTS is billed separately.
API token requests pay the full calculated price and do not consume free uses.
Anonymous V1 audio must have a valid server-probed duration of at most 10 seconds; no client duration fallback is accepted.
For logged-in and API V1 requests, missing probe duration retains the request duration and then 1-second billing fallback; probe exceptions still fail.

Portrait moderation and consent requirements are unchanged.

post.description:
Generate a pre-signed PUT URL for direct browser/client upload.
If bucket is omitted, files are uploaded to 3days-apac by default. The returned uploadUrl may use R2 or Amazon S3 and contains the authentication needed for the PUT; an S3 upload's cdnUrl is served through CloudFront. Use the returned uploadUrl and cdnUrl without reconstructing or changing their hosts, paths or query strings.
urlPrefix requests a leading object-key path.
cdnDomain requests a CDN domain suffix for R2 uploads.
Site runtimes reject urlPrefix and cdnDomain overrides to preserve isolated storage routing.
The returned logical key is scoped to {urlPrefix}/{env}/user/{user_id}/. CloudFront URLs and physical S3 object keys additionally include the jp-s3/{bucket}/ routing prefix.
Use cdnUrl as the public file URL after the PUT upload succeeds.
API-token calls are charged per successfully issued presigned URL using the current `r2` entry from GET /v1/feature-pricing; this is not a per-byte upload charge. The balance is checked before URL generation and debited after the URL is created.
The subsequent client PUT is separate. A failed PUT does not automatically refund the presigning fee; requesting a replacement URL can incur another fee. Normal logged-in web/app calls are free.
PUT upload contract (also applies to the legacy alias):
- Only the A2E request for this URL uses Authorization: Bearer. Send the raw file bytes to uploadUrl with HTTP PUT; do not use JSON or multipart/form-data.
- The uploadUrl query already authenticates the PUT. Use a separate unauthenticated HTTP client: do not forward Authorization or manually add x-amz-* headers.
- Send Content-Type matching the requested contentType. Preserve the complete uploadUrl, including all query bytes and its storage host; do not rewrite it to cdnUrl.
- fileSize and contentLength are optional outside site runtimes. Omit them for a minimal upload; never copy a placeholder byte count.
- If you provide a positive integer size, Content-Length must equal that actual file byte count. Outside site runtimes, contentLength takes priority over fileSize; site runtimes ignore contentLength and always bind the PUT to the validated fileSize. A chunked request without that bound Content-Length will fail for either R2 or S3 uploads.
- Site runtimes can require fileSize; use the actual byte count there. expiresIn is URL validity, not object retention. Use cdnUrl only after PUT succeeds.
- Browser clients may set forceR2=true only when retrying a failed S3 PUT. This bypasses the S3 sample for that replacement upload target.
Two-step cURL example (requires curl and jq):
```sh
curl -X POST "https://api.a2e.ai/v1/r2/upload-presigned-url" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_A2E_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"key":"upload.png","purpose":"STAGING","contentType":"image/png","expiresIn":300}' \
  --fail-with-body --output /tmp/a2e-upload-response.json
upload_url=$(jq -er '.data.uploadUrl' /tmp/a2e-upload-response.json)
curl -X PUT "$upload_url" -H 'Content-Type: image/png' \
  --data-binary @upload.png --fail-with-body
```
Replace YOUR_A2E_API_KEY and upload.png with your own API key and file.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Send an `application/json` body. Required fields: `key`.
### Behavior
- Validates the submitted payload and performs the operation described by the request schema.
- Conditional fields, mutually exclusive inputs, limits, and defaults are enforced as documented by their schemas.
### Response
- On `200`, consume the fields defined by that response schema below.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.
### Errors
- `400` — Bad Request - Invalid parameters.
- `401` — Unauthorized - Invalid or missing JWT token.
### Related Operations
- `POST /v1/r2/get_upload_presigned_url` — Get pre-signed upload URL.

post.description:
Generate a product image by combining product and person images with customizable positioning and styling. This endpoint returns an image, not a video.
**⚠️ IMPORTANT: This is an ASYNCHRONOUS operation**
### Async Workflow
1. **Submit Task** - Call this endpoint to create a new generation task
   - Returns immediately with task `_id` and status `initialized`
   - Task is queued for processing
2. **Processing States** - The task goes through these states:
   - `initialized` → Task created, waiting in queue
   - `sent` → Task submitted to AI service
   - `pending` → Task received by AI service
   - `processing` → AI is generating the image
   - `completed` → Generation finished successfully
   - `failed` → Generation failed (check `failed_message`)
3. **Get Results** - Poll for task status and results:
   - Use `GET /v1/productAvatar/{_id}` to check status
   - Use `GET /v1/productAvatar/allRecords` to list all tasks
   - When `current_status` is `completed`, `result_image_url` contains the generated image
4. **Timeout Handling**:
   - Tasks timeout after 2 hours and automatically fail
   - Credits are automatically refunded on timeout or failure
### Best Practices
- Poll every 3-5 seconds to check task status
- Handle both `completed` and `failed` states
- Store the returned `_id` to query results later.
### Request
- This operation permits anonymous requests. Authenticated callers may send a bearer token.
- Supply `x-anonymous-id` headers as documented in the parameter schema, including any anonymous identity requirements.

**Modes:**
- `text-to-video` – generate video from text prompt
- `image-to-video` – generate video from an image (+ optional end frame in PRO)

post.description:
Generate videos using Kling Omni API (model: kling-v3-omni).
This is a simplified wrapper around the official Kling API.
**Key Features:**
- Multi-reference images: up to 7 images, use `<<<image_N>>>` tags in prompt
- Multi-shot editing: AI Director (intelligence) or manual (customize) storyboard
- Native sound generation via `sound` parameter
- Flexible duration: 3–15 seconds
**Simplified vs Official API:**
- `image_list`: accepts `string[]` (image URLs); official uses `[{image_url, type?}]`, auto-converted on server
- `sound`: accepts `boolean`; official uses `"on"/"off"`, auto-converted on server
- `multi_prompt`: items need `prompt` + `duration`; server auto-adds `index` field for official API
- `prompt` is required when `multi_shot=false` or `shot_type=intelligence`
- `multi_prompt` total duration must equal `duration` when `shot_type=customize`
- `element_ids`: `string[]` of Element `asset_id` values (not `_id`). Create an Element with `POST /v1/klingAssets/elements` (`name`, frontal `image_url`, 1–3 `reference_image_urls`), poll `GET /v1/klingAssets` until `status` is `succeed`, then pass its `asset_id`. With `image_list`, at most 3 Elements are allowed.
Actual media size, dimensions, duration, format and applicable frame-rate limits are checked against the selected provider interface before charging or creating any task. Client metadata is not authoritative. Invalid or unreadable media returns HTTP 400 with the failing field, measured value and expected range; direct API requests are not automatically resized or transcoded and do not inherit lower website upload limits.
Media inspection errors preserve HTTP status and business code: 400 INVALID_MEDIA for confirmed invalid media, 400 MEDIA_RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for inaccessible or expired sources, 400 MEDIA_PROBE_LIMIT for the server source inspection budget, 429 MEDIA_PROBE_BUSY for local queue saturation, 503 MEDIA_PROBE_UNAVAILABLE for transient network/upstream failures, 504 MEDIA_PROBE_TIMEOUT for inspection timeouts, and 500 MEDIA_PROBE_FAILED for internal processing failures. All media checked for this request share a 280-second deadline, including queueing, Range probing and full-download fallback. Even valid assets can exceed this processing deadline. Timeout cancels remaining inspection and cleanup completes before returning; no automatic retry, charge, task creation or generation-provider submission occurs on failed inspection.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Send an `application/json` body when using the optional controls documented in the request schema.
- API-token callers may include `webhook_url` and `webhook_token` for best-effort terminal-state notifications; ordinary JWT/cookie calls ignore these fields.
### Behavior
- This is an asynchronous operation: a successful submission creates a task and returns before processing finishes.
- Persist the returned task identifier and use the corresponding detail or list operation to observe progress.
- Treat the detail endpoint as the source of truth even when webhook delivery is enabled.
### Response
- A `200` response confirms task acceptance; it does not by itself mean media generation has completed.
- Retain the returned identifier and wait for a documented terminal status before using output URLs.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.
### Errors
- `400` — Invalid parameters, or ELEMENT_RECREATION_REQUIRED for incomplete Element media references outside the legacy native compatibility exception. Missing primary images and malformed reference metadata are not covered by that exception.
- `401` — Unauthorized - Invalid or missing JWT token.
- `429` — MEDIA_PROBE_BUSY - Local media inspection queue is full or its wait deadline elapsed.
- `500` — MEDIA_PROBE_FAILED - Internal media inspection failure; not a media specification violation.
- `503` — MEDIA_PROBE_UNAVAILABLE - Transient network or upstream failure; retry is allowed.
- `504` — MEDIA_PROBE_TIMEOUT - Media connection, download, inspection or the shared 280-second request inspection deadline elapsed; retry is allowed. This is a processing timeout, not a media specification violation.
### Related Operations
- `GET /v1/klingOmni/allRecords` — Get all Kling Omni video records.
- `GET /v1/klingOmni/{_id}` — Get Kling Omni video detail.
- `PUT /v1/klingOmni/{_id}` — Update Kling Omni video name.

Poll this endpoint with data._id from the start response. When data.current_status is completed, read the generated video from data.result_url. The task includes its stored refund status; missing refund state is unknown.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Supply `_id` in the URL path.
### Behavior
- Retrieves the current server-side representation of the requested resource or task.
- For asynchronous tasks, inspect the documented status and result fields before consuming generated media.
- Repeat the request only as needed for polling and stop after the task reaches a terminal state.
### Response
- On `200`, consume the fields defined by that response schema below.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.
### Errors
- `401` — Unauthorized - Invalid or missing JWT token.
- `404` — Task not found for the authenticated user.
- `429` — Task query budget exceeded; retry after the Retry-After response header.
- `503` — Task query budget temporarily unavailable; retry after the Retry-After response header.
### Related Operations
- `GET /v1/userWan30/allRecords` — List Wan3.0 video tasks.
- `DELETE /v1/userWan30/{_id}` — Delete a Wan3.0 video task.
- `POST /v1/userWan30/start` — Start Wan3.0 all-in-one video generation.

Authentication: set header Authorization: Bearer <token> (supports user JWT or sk_ API token).

delete.description:
Delete the authenticated user's Wan3.0 task record identified by _id.
### Request
- Send a valid bearer token. The server evaluates the operation in the authenticated caller's access context.
- Supply `_id` in the URL path.
### Behavior
- Deletes or marks the selected resource as deleted according to the endpoint's documented lifecycle rules.
- Use the resource identifier from a list, creation, or detail response; deleting one resource does not affect unrelated records.
- Do not assume an in-progress task can be cancelled unless the endpoint explicitly documents that behavior.
### Response
- A `200` response confirms that the deletion request was applied to the selected record.
- JSON object responses, including error responses, normally carry a top-level `trace_id` string for this request; include it when contacting support. It is not a task identifier.
- Do not infer undocumented fields or statuses; clients should tolerate additional response properties.
### Errors
- `401` — Unauthorized - Invalid or missing JWT token.

- `GET /v1/userWan30/{_id}` — Get Wan3.0 video task details.

tags.name: Miscellaneous
tags.description: Supporting utilities including file upload to cloud storage, pre-signed URL generation, URL saving, and other helper endpoints used across API workflows.

tags.name: Generate Avatar Videos
tags.description: Submit a script or audio file to generate an avatar presentation video. The digital avatar lip-syncs to your content and speaks on your behalf.

tags.name: TTS and Voice Clone
tags.description: Convert text to natural-sounding speech using a library of built-in voices, or clone a custom voice from a short audio sample for consistent narration.

tags.name: Create Avatars
tags.description: Train and manage custom digital avatars from uploaded video recordings. Trained avatars can then be used in avatar video generation workflows.

tags.name: Background Library
tags.description: Add, list, and delete images in the custom background library. For image subject cutout, use the separate Image Background Removal API.

tags.name: Video Twin
tags.description: Build a personalised video twin - a digital double trained on your own footage - that can speak and present content on your behalf with natural motion.

tags.name: Face Swap
tags.description: Swap faces between a source and a target image or video with identity-preserving blending. Handles diverse lighting, pose, and expression conditions.

tags.name: AI Dubbing
tags.description: Automatically translate and re-dub a video into a target language using voice cloning and AI-driven lip-sync adjustment.

tags.name: Caption Removal
tags.description: Detect and cleanly remove embedded captions, subtitles, or text overlays from video frames using AI inpainting.

tags.name: Upscale
tags.description: Enhance the resolution of images and videos using AI super-resolution. Sharpens fine detail and reduces compression artifacts without visible upscale noise.

tags.name: Text to Image
tags.description: Generate images from natural language prompts using the platform's diffusion model pipeline. Describe what you want - style, composition, lighting - and receive high-resolution results.

tags.name: Nano Banana
tags.description: Image generation powered by Google Gemini's image model. Accepts text-only prompts or text combined with up to four reference images for high-fidelity, semantically-aware output.

tags.name: Photobook
tags.description: Produce a series of stylised portrait photos with consistent subject identity across different poses, outfits, or backgrounds.

tags.name: GPT Image
tags.description: Image generation and editing via OpenAI GPT-4o image capabilities. Excels at precise instruction-following, photorealistic rendering, and multi-step image editing tasks.

tags.name: Wan2.6 Image
tags.description: Generate images with the Wan 2.6 image model using text prompts and configurable output dimensions.

tags.name: Wan2.7 Image
tags.description: Generate images with the Wan 2.7 image model using text prompts and configurable output dimensions.

tags.name: Qwen Image
tags.description: Generate and edit images with Qwen Image models using text prompts and optional reference images.

tags.name: Flux 2
tags.description: High-quality image generation using the Flux 2 Pro model. Delivers strong results for both creative and photorealistic use cases with fast inference.

tags.name: Kling Image
tags.description: Generate high-fidelity images with Kling using prompt, aspect ratio, resolution, and optional reference-image controls.

tags.name: Image Edit
tags.description: Edit product images with the product mode. The clothing mode is deprecated; use Virtual Try-On for garment previews. This endpoint does not provide inpainting or outpainting.

tags.name: Image to Video
tags.description: Convert a still image into an AI-animated video. Control motion intensity, duration, and aspect ratio to produce smooth, high-quality video clips from a single reference image.

tags.name: Wan Image to Video
tags.description: Animate a still image into a video using the Wan 2.5 / 2.6 open-source video diffusion model family. Part of the Wan series known for fluid motion and temporal consistency.

tags.name: Wan 2.6 R2V Flash
tags.description: Generate a video from reference images with the fast Wan 2.6 reference-to-video workflow.

tags.name: HappyHorse Video
tags.description: Asynchronous video generation powered by HappyHorse models on Alibaba DashScope. Supports HappyHorse 1.0 and 1.1 for text-to-video, image-to-video, and reference-to-video; video-edit remains on HappyHorse 1.0. HappyHorse 1.1 generation supports 480P, 720P, or 1080P; 1.0 and video-edit support 720P or 1080P.

tags.name: Talking Photo
tags.description: Animate a portrait photo to lip-sync with a given audio track, generating a realistic talking-head video from a single still image.

tags.name: Talking Video
tags.description: Re-lip-sync an existing video to a new audio source using AI-driven facial animation and motion warping.

tags.name: Virtual Try-On
tags.description: Generate a realistic preview of a person wearing a specific garment from a product image - no physical samples required.

tags.name: ThinkSound
tags.description: Generate semantically-aware ambient sound effects and background audio that match the visual content of a video clip.

tags.name: Motion Transfer
tags.description: Transfer body motion captured in a source video onto a target subject, preserving the target's appearance and background.

tags.name: Actor Swap
tags.description: Replace an actor in a video segment with a different person, retaining original motion, camera angle, and scene continuity.

tags.name: Product Avatar
tags.description: Generate a product image using a product photo, a person photo, and product_rect placement coordinates. The completed task returns result_image_url.

tags.name: Head Swap
tags.description: Replace the head in an image with a target face while keeping the original body, clothing, lighting, and background intact.

tags.name: Veo Video
tags.description: Text-to-video generation powered by Google DeepMind's Veo model. Produces high-definition, cinematic video clips from a text prompt or a reference image.

tags.name: Kling Video
tags.description: Text-to-video and image-to-video generation with Kling. Recognized for smooth motion dynamics, scene consistency, and high visual fidelity.

tags.name: Kling Omni
tags.description: An extended variant of Kling with additional control parameters for output style, generation quality, and advanced scene handling.

tags.name: Grok Video
tags.description: Video generation using xAI's Grok model. Suitable for creative and coherent video synthesis from descriptive text prompts.

tags.name: Hailuo Video Generation
tags.description: Generate videos with Hailuo from text prompts or image references with configurable duration and output settings.

tags.name: Seedance 1.5 Pro
tags.description: Generate cinematic videos with Seedance 1.5 Pro from a text prompt, a first-frame image, or first and last frames. Supports configurable duration, aspect ratio, resolution, camera behavior, and audio generation.

tags.name: Wan3.0 Video Generation
tags.description: Generate Wan 3.0 videos from text, first-frame images, first and last frames, or image, video, and audio references. Query the returned task ID to read its status and result_url.
